- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.0) or shows strong bearish signals, model often overshoots downward; avoid aggressive downward revisions; consider mean reversion bias.
- After a recent price spike, model frequently overcorrects downward — apply a “lag correction”: delay full reversal until 2–3 periods after peak.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often fails to capture mean reversion — use 10–15 day moving average as a baseline for adjustment.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to overconfidence in short-term momentum — reduce forecast volatility if sentiment is weak or trending sideways.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1 → -1 → +1), model tends to misjudge turning points — apply a 2-period smoothing filter to sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- Avoid forecasting below 70% of recent 10-day low if sentiment is neutral or negative — model often underestimates downside risk in flat sentiment periods.
